title: Warning of a breach served by bailiff; petition mid-way through the one-month period

expect.why: The breach may not be relied on 'إلا اذا تواصل ارتكابها أو تجديدها لاكثر من شهر بعد انذار المؤجر'. Warning on 2026-06-15, one month ends on the same day number, 2026-07-15. On 2026-06-29 the month has certainly not run under any counting, so the lessor cannot yet rely on the breach. 'inTime' here means: the waiting month has not yet passed.

title: One day before the end of the one-month period after the warning

expect.why: The text does not settle this: 'لاكثر من شهر بعد انذار المؤجر' says neither whether the day of the warning counts nor whether the last day counts, and the texts given hold no general counting article. Likelier reading (the warning day not counted, the month ends on the same day number): last day 2026-07-15. Other reading (the warning day counted): last day 2026-07-14, so this petition would be on the last day. On either reading the month is not yet over on 2026-07-14, but the rule must warn, not decide.

title: Petition on the day the one-month period after the warning ends

expect.why: The text does not settle this: 'more than one month after the warning' does not say whether the breach may be relied on on the very day the month ends. Likelier reading: last day 2026-07-15 (same day number), so the petition is on the last day and the breach is not yet 'more than a month'. Other reading: last day 2026-07-14 (warning day counted), so the month is already over. The rule must warn.

title: One day after the one-month period after the warning

expect.why: The text does not settle this. Likelier reading: month ended 2026-07-15, so on 2026-07-16 the breach has continued 'لاكثر من شهر' and may be relied on. Other reading, if the last day also is not counted (more than one month must be complete): last day 2026-07-16, the petition is on it. The text does not say. The rule must warn, not decide.

title: Two weeks after the one-month period after the warning has ended

expect.why: Warning 2026-06-15; one month ends 2026-07-15 (at the latest 2026-07-16 on any counting; weekday of 07-15 is a Wednesday, no rest day involved). 2026-07-30 is fourteen days past it, beyond every reading, so the waiting month has passed and the breach, if it continued, may be relied on ('late' here means: the period has passed).

title: Warning on the 31st; the next month has 30 days

expect.why: The text does not settle this: 'شهر' from 31 August has no 31 September and the texts give no month-end rule. Likelier reading: the month ends on the last day of September, 2026-09-30, so the petition is on the last day. Other reading: 31 September overflows to 2026-10-01, so the petition is one day before the last day. The rule must warn.

title: Warning on the 30th of January; February is short

expect.why: The text does not settle this: one month from 30 January has no 30 February (2026 is not a leap year) and the texts give no month-end rule. Likelier reading: the month ends on the last day of February, 2026-02-28, so 2026-03-02 is after it (a weekly-rest day or later extension would reach at most 2026-03-01). Other reading: 30 February overflows to 2026-03-02, so the petition is on the last day. The rule must warn.

title: One-month period ends on a Friday; petition on the Sunday after

expect.why: Warning 2026-06-10, the month ends 2026-07-10, a Friday. The texts given do not say which days are weekly rest days and hold no rule that a period ending on a rest day runs to the next working day. Reading without extension: last day 2026-07-10, the petition is two days after. Reading with extension (Friday and Saturday rest): last day Sunday 2026-07-12, the petition is on it; (Friday only): 2026-07-11. The rule must warn.

title: One-month period ends on 5 July, a national holiday

expect.why: Warning 2026-06-05, the month ends 2026-07-05 (a Sunday, a date commonly an official holiday). The texts given do not name any official holiday and hold no extension rule. Reading without extension: last day 2026-07-05, the petition is one day after. Reading with extension to the next working day: 2026-07-06, the petition is on the last day. The rule must warn.

title: Warning of a breach sent only by registered letter

expect.why: 'ويجب أن يتم هذا الانذار والا كان باطلا بعقد غير قضائى مع ايضاح السبب'. The warning must be made by an extrajudicial act (a bailiff's act); the same Code names the registered letter separately where it allows it (188 ¶4, 192 ¶2), and does not here. A letter alone therefore does not satisfy the step and the month counts from nothing. Note: the reason stated in the warning and the reproduction of the paragraph cannot be set by a slot.

title: Warning of a breach served by bailiff, more than a month ago

expect.why: A warning 'بعقد غير قضائى' (bailiff) on 2026-06-15 and a month that ended on 2026-07-15 well before the petition: the step is done as far as means and date are concerned. The statement of the reason and the reproduction of the paragraph's content, also required on pain of nullity, cannot be set by a slot.

title: Notice to pay rent; petition inside the month; rent fell due earlier

expect.why: 'لا ينتج أثره الا بعد مرور شهر واحد من الاخطار بالدفع الذى يبقى بدون نتيجة': the month runs from the notice to pay, not from the due date. Notice 2026-05-20, month ends 2026-06-20 (a Saturday). On 2026-06-15 the month has not passed on any counting: the rescission clause has no effect yet. Counted wrongly from the due date (2026-04-10) the month would already have passed, which is the other answer.

title: Notice to pay rent; petition the day after the month, a Sunday

expect.why: Notice 2026-05-20, the month ends on the same day number, 2026-06-20, a Saturday. The text does not say whether the notice day counts, whether the last day counts, or whether a period ending on a rest day runs to the next working day (and the texts do not say which days are rest days). Likelier reading: last day 2026-06-20, so 2026-06-21 is one day after. Other readings: 2026-06-19 (notice day counted) or 2026-06-21 (extension past Saturday, or Friday and Saturday rest). The rule must warn.

title: Notice to pay rent; petition well after the month

expect.why: Notice 2026-05-20; one month ends 2026-06-20 (at the latest 2026-06-22 on any reading). 2026-07-20 is a month after, so the waiting month has passed and, the notice having stayed without result, the clause may take effect ('late' here means: the period has passed).

title: Lease made before the 2005 reform; no notice to quit served

expect.why: 'لا ينتهي إيجار المحلات الخاصة بهذه الأحكام إلا بأثر تنبيه بالإخلاء ... وفي مدة ستة أشهر قبل الأجل على الأقل'; without it (173 ¶2) the written lease continues by tacit extension. The contract of 1998 is before any publication in 2005, so 187 مكرر (no notice needed) does not apply to it, and 187 مكرر 1 leaves it under the earlier rules. Not done, no exemption: the step is missing.

title: Pre-reform lease; notice to quit by bailiff, but the end of the term is not known

expect.why: The form is right ('عقد غير قضائي'), but the notice must come 'قبل الأجل' by at least six months, and no slot holds the date the term ends. The rule cannot say the step is done and must ask for that date (a rule must not say 'done' while the timing is still open). Reasons stated in the notice and the reproduction of 194 also cannot be set by a slot.

title: Pre-reform lease; notice to quit sent only by registered letter

expect.why: 'ويجب أن يتم التنبيه بالإخلاء بعقد غير قضائي ... وإلا اعتبر باطلا'. The notice to quit must be an extrajudicial act (bailiff); a registered letter is not named here, though the Code names it in other articles (188 ¶4, 192 ¶2). The notice is void, so the step counts as not taken.

title: Pre-reform lease; notice to quit by 'another means'

expect.why: The text requires 'عقد غير قضائي' but does not say which other means are extrajudicial acts besides a bailiff's. 'Another means' may or may not be one. The text does not settle this; the rule must warn and not decide.

title: Pre-reform lease; whether a notice to quit was served is unknown

expect.why: The regime applies (contract of 1998) and the notice to quit is required for the lease to end; whether it was served is unknown, and an unknown fact is not a 'no': the rule asks.

title: Lease made well after the reform; no notice to quit

expect.why: 'يلزم المستأجر بمغادرة الأمكنة المستأجرة بانتهاء الأجل المحدد في العقد دون حاجة إلى توجيه تنبيه بالإخلاء': for a lease made after the publication (which was in 2005; a contract of 2012 is certainly after), no notice to quit is needed unless the parties stipulated otherwise. Nothing in the case says they did.

title: Lease made after the reform; the contract sets notice terms

expect.why: The no-notice rule applies 'ما لم يشترط الأطراف خلاف ذلك'. The slot says the contract sets a form, period or addressee for notice before a claim, which may or may not amount to stipulating that a notice to quit is needed. The text does not settle whether such a clause revives the notice; the rule must warn, not decide.

title: Lease made in 2005, the publication day not known

expect.why: 187 مكرر applies to leases made 'ابتداء من تاريخ نشر هذا القانون في الجريدة الرسمية'. The texts give no publication date; the reform is of 2005 but the day within the year is not in the texts. A lease of 2005-06-15 may fall on either side. The rule must warn, not decide which regime applies.

title: Commercial lease; the date of the contract is not known

expect.why: Whether a notice to quit is needed (173) or not (187 مكرر ¶2) depends on whether the lease was made before or after the publication; the date is unknown, so the rule asks for contract_date.

title: The lease is not one governed by the commercial-code lease provisions

expect.why: 'تطبـق الأحكام الآتيـــة على إيجار العمارات أو المحلات التي يستغل فيها محل تجاري': the notice-to-quit rule of 173 reaches only leases of premises where a business is run. If the lease is not one, the step does not apply and its absence is not a defect under these articles.

title: Whether the lease is a commercial lease is not known

expect.why: Whether 169 reaches the premises (a business is run in them, registered as the text requires) is unknown, and so is whether 173 applies. The rule must ask, not treat unknown as 'no'.

title: Lease of premises owned by a commune or other public administrative body

expect.why: 170 ¶4 applies the lease provisions to premises of the State, wilayas, communes and public bodies if they meet 169, subject to 185 and 186 (no refusal without the eviction compensation). The texts say nothing about which court hears the dispute, ordinary or administrative; they say only 'الجهة القضائية المختصة' (194). They do not settle whether this case leaves the ordinary courts. The rule must warn, not decide.

title: Lessee is a public economic enterprise, not a public administrative body

expect.why: 170 ¶3 puts the lease of premises needed by public economic enterprises under the same provisions 'في حدود القوانين والأنظمة التي تسودها'. The party is not a public administrative body (slot 'no'), so nothing takes the case out of the ordinary rules: a pre-reform lease with no notice to quit is a missing step as in the ordinary case. Contrast with the case where a public administrative body is a party.
